proof_roadmap: Approximate the pair of maps by a finitely presented model (proof lines 4577-4590).

difficulty_reason: For ring maps R to A to B with R to B of finite type and A to B faithfully flat and of finite presentation, the lemma asserts that R to A is of finite type (statement lines 4568-4573). The proof is a small approximation argument. A cited algebra result produces a commutative diagram whose bottom row is the given sequence and whose top row R to A_0 to B_0 has R to A_0 of finite presentation, A_0 to B_0 faithfully flat of finite presentation and B equal to the tensor product of A and B_0 over A_0 (proof lines 4577-4590). Because R to B is of finite type, one may add finitely many elements to A_0 in such a way that B_0 to B becomes surjective, which is the step where the finite type hypothesis enters (proof lines 4590-4592). In that situation the base change of the map A_0 to A along A_0 to B_0 is isomorphic to the surjective map B_0 to B, and faithful flatness lets surjectivity descend, so A_0 to A is surjective; composing with the finite presentation of R to A_0 gives finite type for R to A (proof lines 4593-4598). The claim is H2: the approximation diagram, the enlargement of A_0 to force surjectivity and the descent of surjectivity along a faithfully flat map are three separate steps that have to be carried out, and the display of the isomorphism of the two base changed maps is the crux.
